headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage/cascading error: next-ai-draw-io can use MCP and broad egress, while whisper is local-only with no filesystem or network access.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A can use MCP and browsers, so it may ingest external content; B is command-line local-only with no clipboard, MCP, or browser surface. There is no documented shared channel between them, so prompt injection is limited to unusual manual bridging rather than a default pairwise pathway.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies A-generated text into B as instructions, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared MCP server is introduced between the agents, the pathway widens.
mitigations: Disable manual copy-paste of untrusted A output into B.
Keep B isolated from any shared MCP server.
Use a fixed prompt template for B that ignores instruction-like text in inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A handles PDFs, text, images, and API keys, but B cannot read files, write files, or egress network traffic. Because B has no filesystem or network surfaces, A's sensitive inputs are not plausibly exposed through the pair by default.
conditions: IF B is wrapped by an external orchestrator that injects A's files into B's prompt, leakage increases.
IF B is replaced with a networked or file-reading variant, the assessment changes.
mitigations: Keep A's API keys out of shared prompts.
Do not pass raw documents from A into B unless redacted.
Run B in a separate process with no file mounts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has broad network egress and browser/MCP use, while B has no filesystem write, no shell, no subprocesses, and no network egress. The profiles do not show overlapping mutable resources, so there is no plausible write-write conflict in the default pair.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, conflict could emerge.
IF B is replaced with a writable variant, the conflict analysis changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid granting shared git or filesystem write access.
Use read-only mounts for any common inputs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can generate diagram content from documents and external model calls; B is a speech model that could be used downstream to transcribe or render A's output, but B has no documented verification or action-taking authority. The pathway exists if an operator chains A into B, yet the lack of default integration keeps this below high.
conditions: IF A's generated text is fed into B as authoritative source text, errors can cascade.
IF an operator uses B to publish or summarize A output without review, downstream mistakes propagate.
mitigations: Require human review between A and B.
Mark A output as untrusted in the handoff note.
Use B only for transcription, not factual validation.

E_compliance.rationale: A requests API keys and broad egress to multiple third-party AI services, while B is local-only and handles audio/speech. The mismatch is mainly retention and residency risk for A's outbound data; B is not cited for residency because it has no network or secret-handling surface in the profile.
conditions: IF A processes regulated documents through third-party APIs, residency or retention obligations may be triggered.
IF the operator routes personal data into A's external model calls, compliance controls must be checked.
mitigations: Restrict A to approved providers only.
Redact regulated fields before sending documents to A.
Document retention settings for each external API.
Keep B offline and local-only for any regulated audio.
